title: Accounts Assistant
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Assistant

This is an excellent opportunity for an Accounts Assistant to join a busy Finance team in a genuinely varied, all-round role. Around 50% of the position will focus on Credit Control, with the remainder covering Sales Ledger, credit card reconciliations, CIS returns, accruals, reporting and month-end processes.

The business is looking for someone who wants to develop their career within Finance, take ownership of their responsibilities and become a long-term member of the team.

About the Role

As an Accounts Assistant, you'll support the wider Finance function across both transactional accounting and Credit Control activities. You'll manage your own portfolio of customer accounts, including larger clients with multiple sites, while also supporting the wider team with day-to-day accounting and month-end responsibilities.

The role will involve approximately 50% Credit Control, including chasing outstanding debt, monitoring credit limits, completing credit checks and managing customer accounts. You'll also support the Sales Ledger, process invoices and credit notes, reconcile payments and assist with the preparation of monthly financial information.

This is a fully office-based position within a collaborative Finance team, offering excellent exposure across different areas of accounting and the opportunity to develop your skills over the long term.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage Credit Control activities across a portfolio of key customer accounts.
- Chase outstanding debts and maintain positive, professional customer relationships.
- Allocate incoming customer payments and accurately reconcile cash receipts.
- Monitor customer accounts, credit limits and overall account exposure.
- Complete credit checks for new clients and support the set-up of new customer accounts.
- Prepare and issue new client welcome letters.
- Upload invoices to customer portals and manage portal-based billing requirements.
- Maintain the Sales Ledger, including raising invoices, processing credit notes and resolving account queries.
- Reconcile and process company credit card statements.
- Prepare monthly financial reports and information for Directors.
- Complete monthly CIS returns and submit P32 returns in line with HMRC requirements.
- Prepare and process month-end accruals.
- Assist with month-end and year-end accounting processes.
- Complete monthly and quarterly compliance checks.
- Support the preparation of information required for external audits.
- Provide day-to-day accounting and administrative support to the wider Finance team.

Key Requirements
- Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Assistant Accountant, Sales Ledger or similar all-round Finance role.
- Previous Credit Control experience, or a willingness to take ownership of a significant Credit Control responsibility.
- Good understanding of Sales Ledger processes, including invoicing, payments and reconciliations.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office.
- Experience using Sage is desirable.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good organisational and time management skills.
- Confident communicator with the ability to build positive relationships with customers and colleagues.
- Proactive and solutions-focused approach to resolving queries and managing accounts.
- Reliable and enthusiastic team player who is comfortable working in a fully office-based environment.
- Genuine interest in developing a broader accounting skill set and progressing within Finance.
- Willingness to learn, take ownership and become a long-term member of the team.

What's on Offer
- Salary circa £30,000, depending on experience.
- Permanent opportunity within an established and independently owned business.
- Broad, all-round Accounts Assistant role with significant exposure to Credit Control and wider accounting.
- Opportunity to take ownership of your own portfolio of customer accounts.
- Excellent exposure to Sales Ledger, CIS, month-end, reporting and compliance.
- Supportive Finance team and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunity for long-term development and progression.
- Fully office-based working environment.
- Monday to Thursday, 8:30am-5:00pm, and Friday, 8:30am-4:00pm.
- Opportunity to join a business with clear values and a strong focus on delivering quality service.
- Long-term opportunity to develop your career within a growing and established business.

Are you an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys building relationships, resolving queries and finding solutions rather than simply chasing outstanding payments?

This is a great opportunity to join an established, supportive Credit Control team within a professional working environment where people genuinely enjoy working together.

The vacancy has arisen following an internal promotion into another area of Finance, which gives a good indication of the opportunities available for those looking to develop their careers.

You will be joining a knowledgeable, friendly team with a supportive manager, structured training and the opportunity to build relationships with a wide range of internal stakeholders and clients.

A great opportunity for the right person

There is plenty to like about this opportunity, particularly if you enjoy the relationship-building side of Credit Control.

What makes this opportunity attractive?
- A supportive, established team: Join a settled Credit Control department of 11 people, with a good mix of experience and a collaborative approach.
- Career development: The vacancy has arisen through internal progression, with opportunities to develop your skills and potentially move into other areas of Finance in the future.
- More than just debt chasing: Build relationships, investigate queries, negotiate payment arrangements and work with internal stakeholders to find solutions.
- Variety and exposure: Work with different clients and colleagues across the business, developing your communication and stakeholder management skills.
- A supportive manager: Benefit from clear guidance, structured onboarding and a team that is happy to share knowledge.
- Professional development: Potential opportunities for further training and qualification support.
- Hybrid working: Enjoy a balance of office collaboration and working from home once you have completed your initial training.

This is a role where your ability to communicate, build trust and resolve problems will be just as important as your ability to collect outstanding debt.

The role will involve

Working as part of the wider Credit Control team, you will take responsibility for managing overdue client balances and helping to ensure payments are received promptly.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Proactively contacting clients by telephone and email to chase outstanding payments.
- Building positive relationships with clients and internal stakeholders.
- Investigating outstanding queries and working with colleagues to resolve payment delays.
- Negotiating payment arrangements and following up on agreed commitments.
- Monitoring aged debt and taking appropriate action to reduce overdue balances.
- Maintaining accurate records of collection activity and payment commitments.
- Assisting with monthly statements, credit control correspondence and reporting.
- Working with the wider Finance team to resolve unallocated payments and account queries.

There is a good balance of independent responsibility and teamwork, with plenty of opportunity to interact with colleagues across the wider business.

What are they looking for?

You will already have experience working in Credit Control and be confident managing overdue accounts, communicating with customers and resolving queries.

More importantly, you will be someone who enjoys working with people and understands the importance of maintaining positive relationships while achieving results.

Ideally, you will bring:
- Previous Credit Control experience.
- Confidence chasing overdue payments and negotiating payment arrangements.
- Strong communication skills, both over the telephone and in writing.
- The ability to build relationships with customers and internal stakeholders.
- A proactive, organised approach to managing your workload.

- Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to investigate queries.
- A collaborative attitude and a genuine willingness to support the wider team.

The practical details
- Salary: Up to £29,000.

- Contract: Permanent.

- Hybrid working: 3 days in the office and 2 days from home following initial training.

description:
The Payroll Administrator is fully accountable for the accurate, timely and compliant delivery of payroll for KDB UK employees. The role manages all payroll activities from data collection and validation through to payroll processing, statutory reporting, reconciliations and employee support, ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time.

Working closely with Finance, People & Communications and external payroll providers, the Payroll Administrator maintains payroll records, ensures compliance with UK legislation and supports continuous improvement of payroll processes.

Compliance & Governance
- Ensure payroll activities comply with UK legislation, HMRC requirements and company policies and maintain accurate payroll records and audit trails.

- Act as the primary point of contact for payroll queries and provide timely and professional support to employees and managers regarding pay, deductions, pensions and payroll processes.

- Reconcile payroll reports with finance records.

- Maintain payroll data integrity across HR and payroll systems.
- Identify opportunities to improve payroll accuracy, efficiency and compliance.
- Support payroll system updates, testing and process documentation.

Other Administration
- Support the Fleet Management administration alongside the external supplier
- Ownership of parking management for engineers
- Supporting People & Communications team with onboarding and offboarding
- Manage vetting processes for employees
- Support in the administration for corporate phone supplier
- General admin support of the P&C Business Partner

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Essential
- Proven payroll administration experience with end-to-end payroll accountability, and strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation and HMRC requirements
- Experience managing payroll through an outsourced payroll provider
- Knowledge of pension administration and benefits processing
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy, together with strong Excel and payroll systems skills
- Ability to manage confidential information with discretion
- Strong organisational and time management skills

Desirable - CIPP qualification or equivalent payroll certification and experience in a standalone payroll role

What KDB can offer:

We offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday and 8 additional Bank Holidays, 1 volunteering day, Pension Scheme, Development opportunities and development reviews to help you achieve your professional goals. Endless support from experienced leaders within the doors industry, Bonus, Dental Insurance, Medical Insurance, GymFlex Membership, Life Assurance, Cycle to Work Scheme, Long Service Awards, Kone Discounts, 24/7 GP Support & Wellbeing Access and hybrid working.
